subject: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA

Team —

Quick context: Zephyra (contact: Sara Lim) is ready to run a closed pilot for their realtime analytics feature. They want consistent sub-150ms tail latency for ~200 concurrent sessions over short bursts. Their legal and procurement ask for a short-term dedicated capacity reservation to guarantee latency while we validate routing and caching optimizations.

Request summary (ask to Product/Infra/CS/Ops):
- Temporarily reserve a 2-week dedicated slice: target 8 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2 starting Nov 14.
- Grant a temporary autoscale exception so the reserved slice is not preempted by normal fairshare reclamation and can absorb burst traffic up to defined SLA limits.
- Prepare a lightweight SRE runbook (oncall handoff, fallback model variants, circuit breaker thresholds).
- Pricing/discount pathway for a short-term pilot (CS/procurement to coordinate).

Why this matters: this is a top-of-funnel pilot with clear expansion potential (deal DL-8921). If we can make the pilot feel sticky from a latency perspective, they convert to a paid Dedicated contract. I attach a capacity plan and a draft SLA patch we can use for procurement.

Notes: Zephyra is willing to sign a 6-week pilot commitment if we can reduce the requested reserve to 6 GPUs (costs permitting). Please flag constraints.

Next steps I want:
1) Infra: feasibility on reserve + autoscale exception and options for mixed preemptible/dedicated slice.
2) Product: confirm whether 6 GPUs could meet their latency with batching/quantization; if not, we keep 8.
3) CS/procurement: confirm commercial ask and whether Zephyra can sign the 6-week commitment.

Attached: zephyra_pilot_capacity_plan.pdf, sla_condition_patch.docx

Thanks —
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. A few product questions before we lock sizes:

1) Model profile: what architecture and token rate are we planning to run? (Is this a 13B decoder-only for embedding-ish inference, or full 70B chat-style?) A 13B with quantization + batch size 8 will behave very differently than a 70B.
2) Expected QPS and worst-case concurrent sequence length — you mentioned 200 sessions, what's the average request size?
3) Can Zephyra accept one model variant with lower context window to shave memory if we test it? That would make 6 GPUs more plausible.

From Product POV, my preliminary read: if this is 13–20B family and we push NVMe cache + prefix caching for warm prefixes, 6 GPUs might be enough. For anything >30B or large context windows, we should keep 8.

If Provision is constrained, I can prioritize a small experiment: start with 4 dedicated GPUs + 2 preemptible burst nodes under a higher-priority routing policy (if Infra says that path is feasible).

Please put the model profile and representative request traces in a short follow-up so we can model SLO risk.

- Laura
Director, Product (Redwood Console & Serving)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA

Karthik / Laura —

Short answer: feasible with caveats. Current notes from Infra:

- Capacity: us-west-2 has limited contiguous A100 inventory the week of Nov 14. We can commit 4 guaranteed A100-equivalent slots and offer up to 4 additional preemptible nodes (spot-type) that we can pin for short bursts. That gives you the 8 GPU equivalent in practice but with preemption risk on the 4 spot nodes.

- Autoscale exception: The platform permits per-tenant override flags, but they require an engineering change to the reclaim controller for the duration window and a runbook to ensure we don't violate higher-tier reserved contracts. This typically adds ~24–48h of engineering lead time and a small ops cost. If we approve, I estimate a +10% operational surcharge to the pilot rate to cover reservation overhead.

- SRE runbook: I'll need the expected failure modes (model oom, kv-cache miss storm) and the contact rotation. We should also list fallback model variants (smaller model or quantized variant) and a circuit breaker for request rate throttling. Ops can author a minimal runbook in 1–2 business days if we agree on the final size.

Recommendation options:
A) 4 dedicated + 4 preemptible (fastest, lower cost, moderate risk)
B) 6 dedicated + 0 preemptible (higher cost, lower risk)
C) 4 dedicated + 2 preemptible + autoscale exception for temporary pin (compromise)

Action items for me: confirm node flavor (A100 vs A10X equiv), estimate cost delta for each option, and open an engineering approval for the reclaim-controller exception if Product/CS choose option C.

-Markus
VP, Infrastructure

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA

Looping in commercial context: Sara at Zephyra confirmed by phone they can sign a 6-week pilot commitment if we provide a 2-week guaranteed window to validate latency. Their procurement team (procurement@zephyra.ai) needs:
- A one-page SOW describing the reserved slice, start/end dates, and fallback behavior
- A price for the 2-week guaranteed reservation and any premium for autoscale exceptions

Zephyra is price-sensitive but values reliability. If Product can live with 6 GPUs and Infra can do option C, they prefer that because it lowers cost and accelerates start. Sara: "We can go to contract tomorrow if we get an Ops-friendly fallback and a clear SLA scope."

-Neha
Sr. Customer Success Manager

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Strategic pool reallocation proposal — Zephyra pilot + burst SLA

Thanks, all — excellent alignment. Summary and proposed decision:

- Go with compromise C: provision 4 dedicated GPUs + 2 preemptible slots, plus an autoscale exception to allow an additional 2 preemptible pins during the 2-week guaranteed window (effectively giving 6 dedicated-equivalent for bursts).
- Product will confirm model profile and a trimmed context variant ASAP (Laura: can you confirm by EOD Nov 6?).
- Markus/Ops to author a minimal SRE runbook and open the reclaim-controller approval ticket (Markus: please include the estimated +10% surcharge in the ticket).
- Neha will send the one-page SOW to procurement@zephyra.ai and coordinate signatures; Zephyra has indicated a 6-week commitment once we secure the 2-week guaranteed window.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow Nov 6 10:00am PT to finalize the technical runbook and handoff. Calendar invite incoming.

Attachments: zephyra_pilot_capacity_plan.pdf, sla_condition_patch.docx

If anyone objects to the approach, please raise now; otherwise I'll proceed to open the internal procurement and infra tickets.

Best —
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
